name: Ursolic acid
description: Ursolic acid (CAS 77-52-1 ), also known as urson, prunol, and malol, is a pentacyclic triterpenoid acid extracted primarily from apple peel, rosemary, and holy basil. It functions as a bioactive ingredient and antioxidant stabilizer across pharmaceutical formulations and personal care products. In topical cosmetic formulations, it is incorporated into anti-aging creams and serums where its antioxidant activity helps protect against oxidative degradation of the finished product. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a reference compound and active botanical ingredient. It is frequently utilized in standardized herbal extracts and nutraceutical capsules. In personal care, it acts as a surface-modifying agent in scalp treatments and conditioning formulations, where it influences film-forming behavior on skin and hair. As a natural acidulant, it supports pH buffering in botanical-based emulsions requiring mild acid stabilization. This versatile compound is essential for manufacturers seeking high-performance natural additives for complex chemical systems. Ursolic acid is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in multiple purity grades, including 25%, 50%, 90%, and 98%+ HPLC-grade specifications, with higher purities targeting pharmaceutical and analytical applications. Standard packaging ranges from kilogram quantities for formulators to bulk supply for industrial extraction and processing operations.
